runtime.core: Firecracker microVM (open-source VMM originally built by AWS for Lambda/Fargate)
runtime.firecracker_design_notes: ~50k lines of Rust; boots in ~125ms; <5 MiB memory overhead; runs as a single Rust process; uses KVM; jailer provides defense-in-depth; seccomp + Landlock + cgroup limits on the VMM process itself

boot_path.trick: All template creates are INTERNALLY A RESUME of a pre-booted memfile snapshot. 'Creating' a sandbox = restoring a snapshot. Memory pages load lazily via userfaultfd (UFFD); rootfs is COW overlay via NBD; only touched data is fetched from object storage (GCS/S3).
boot_path.origin_node_resume: If the snapshot is still in the local cache, resume avoids object-storage reads (placement prefers the origin node).
boot_path.deferred_rootfs_export: Feature-flagged: ejects writable COW cache during pause, then seals rootfs diff in background (reflink) — moves diff latency off the pause critical path.

snapshot_model.diff_chain: A paused-sandbox snapshot is a NEW BUILD whose memfile/rootfs are stored as diffs against the template it came from. .header files resolve diff chains.
pause_steps: API records snapshot row in Postgres
Orchestrator pauses VM, snapshots it, diffs memory (dirty-page tracking) and rootfs (COW cache) against the template
Snapshot cached locally; async upload to object storage (with retry budget)
snapshot_model.filesystem_only_snapshot: pause({keepMemory:false}) — drops memory, keeps disk; resume performs a cold boot (RebootSandbox); gated by fs-only-resume-api feature flag; auto-resume never takes this path; never silently downgrades.
snapshot_model.auto_pause: Idle sandboxes pause; inbound traffic resumes them via the client-proxy.
snapshot_model.pre_boot_filesystem_recovery: e2fsck -p -E journal_only runs in jail before VM starts when fs_quiesced was false on pause.
snapshot_model.envd_swap: On cold boot, envd binary can be swapped to a newer version (gated by envd-offline-upgrade-target + fs_quiesced). Uses debugfs to swap; never host-kernel mounts the tenant image.

stack_layers.edge: Client-Proxy (Go) on :3002, uses Consul for sandbox→node lookup; terminates web traffic and routes to the correct orchestrator
stack_layers.control_plane: API server in packages/api (Go, Gin REST, port 80); JWT auth via Supabase; OpenTelemetry instrumentation; Ent ORM + sqlc + Redis + ClickHouse; rate-limiting
stack_layers.compute_plane: Orchestrator in packages/orchestrator (Go, gRPC server) on every sandbox node; requires root for KVM + iptables/netlink; packages/sandbox/{fc,network,nbd,template,uffd}/
stack_layers.in_guest: envd daemon inside each microVM, Connect-RPC on port 49983 (process + filesystem APIs); MMDS for sandbox metadata

data_plane.object_storage: GCS / S3 / local (packages/shared/pkg/storage) keyed by buildID: {buildID}/memfile, /rootfs.ext4, /snapfile, /metadata.json + .header indexes

build_path.template_manager: orchestrator binary in build-node mode, gRPC :5008
build_path.templates_vs_snapshots: Templates start faster and use fewer resources (guest OS is RESTARTED before capturing the long-running process so prefetching is more effective). Recommended over snapshots for per-customer / per-project environments.
build_path.layering: fromTemplate('base') to chain templates without rebuilding shared layers

networking.model: Per-sandbox TAP interface into a host bridge; /30 subnet per sandbox
networking.egress: NAT + per-sandbox iptables rules with physdev module for tap isolation
networking.ingress_to_sandbox: Sandbox-domain port binding via edge proxy: port-<sandboxID>.<DOMAIN_NAME>
networking.optional_no_internet: Per-sandbox; allowed via pause+resume lifecycle flag

isolation_primitives: seccomp filter on the VMM process itself (Firecracker-side jailer; documented in Firecracker security.md)
cgroups v1/v2 for resource limits (CPU, memory, PIDs, blkio, devices)
Per-sandbox TAP into host bridge (no host network stack shared)
eBPF egress proxy for syscall/network observability (claimed in user prompt; also documented in Spheron deep-dive)
security_model.guest_internals: Each microVM runs its own Linux kernel + a minimal Ubuntu-derived rootfs; envd daemon inside VM mediates file/process ops from the orchestrator via Connect-RPC; access token validated against MMDS metadata; token is short-lived JWT scoped to team+sandbox

gpu.managed_tier: CPU-only for Sandboxes + Desktop (per Spheron table)
gpu.oss_self_host: GPU via VFIO-PCI passthrough on bare-metal (Firecracker VFIO support; NVIDIA driver 535+; IOMMU enabled); supports A100/H100
gpu.drawbacks: Cloud VMs with nested-virt add 5-15ms overhead and break PCIe passthrough; bare-metal is required for GPU; Modal/Replicate remain stronger for managed GPU

competitive_landscape.positioning: Open-source sandbox standard for AI agents; closest peer to Modal Sandboxes and Daytona; same Firecracker substrate as AWS Lambda and Anthropic Claude Code (per landscape profiles)

firecracker_vs_wasm.e2b_choice: Firecracker — Linux ABI compatibility lets sandboxes run real Python/Node/Rust/CUDA binaries, full Linux distro, system calls; WASM would limit to wasm-target runtimes (WASI). Trade startup speed for ecosystem compatibility.

microvm_vs_gvisor.firecracker: Hardware-virt; full kernel; supports VFIO (GPU); cold-boot ~125ms + snapshot resume 5-30ms
microvm_vs_gvisor.gvisor: User-space kernel interception (runsc); no PCIe passthrough → no real GPU; lighter cold-start on Modal

ux_tradeoffs.per_second_billing: Bills idle time inside the sandbox (Morph notes 15-30% of billed time is idle for interactive agents)
ux_tradeoffs.long_runtime_cap: 1h base, 24h Pro; longer requires pause+resume (state preserved indefinitely)
ux_tradeoffs.no_credits_on_pro_upgrade: Pro $150/mo is a platform fee, not a credit allowance

bottlenecks_and_risks.managed_gpu: E2B managed tier is CPU-only for code interpreter; GPU requires self-hosting on bare-metal with VFIO — Modal and Replicate dominate managed GPU inference
bottlenecks_and_risks.customer_disintermediation: Top customers are LLM labs that can vertically integrate (OpenAI / Anthropic / Mistral). Anthropic reportedly runs Claude Code artifacts on E2B (per landscape profile, not primary customer list). A single roadmap decision at one LLM provider can collapse a material revenue slice.
bottlenecks_and_risks.platform_fork_risk: Vercel Sandbox (2024-2025) is a direct competitor; Google Cloud Run Sandboxes entered preview 2026; hyperscalers could ship comparable primitives.
bottlenecks_and_risks.hidden_cost_perception: Per-second clock keeps running during agent idle windows (the 'idle-time problem'); Morph flags this as the #1 hidden cost; impacts AI-coding products where the user thinks between turns
bottlenecks_and_risks.concentration: Series A disclosed 88% of Fortune 100 signups — but signups ≠ active enterprise revenue. ARR is not publicly disclosed.
